rationale: C18 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Its third section is closely reproduced in the child's third section: both authorize the Attorney General to delegate functions under the order to officers or agencies of the Department of Justice as he deems necessary. Both also concern Attorney General administration of enemy-property functions, reinforcing that the match reflects shared legal machinery rather than generic delegation boilerplate. C25 and C14 are strong secondary candidates because they likewise assign Trading with the Enemy Act or alien-property functions to the Attorney General and contemplate performance through Justice Department designees, but neither matches the child's redelegation clause as closely as C18.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Attorney General may delegate to any officer and agency of the Department of Justice such of his functions under this order as he may deem necessary.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Secretary of State and the Attorney General may each delegate to the other or to any other officer, person, or agency within his respective department such of his functions under this order as he may deem necessary.
shared_material.explanation: This is a highly specific, nearly verbatim redelegation formula, narrowed in the child to the Attorney General and the Department of Justice.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Attorney General shall carry out the functions provided for in that subsection, including the powers, duties, authority and discretion thereby vested in or conferred upon the President
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Attorney General ... shall perform all functions necessary or appropriate to give effect to any such agreement with relation to property subject to the jurisdiction of the United States
shared_material.explanation: Both orders assign the Attorney General operational responsibility for presidential functions involving enemy property, providing a shared substantive administrative framework.

shared_material.child_excerpt: for the purposes of subsection (h) of section 32 of the Trading with the Enemy Act
shared_material.parent_excerpt: shall be administered and disposed of by the Attorney General as vested property pursuant to the said Trading With the Enemy Act, as amended
shared_material.explanation: The common Trading with the Enemy Act context makes the matching delegation and redelegation structure materially probative.
